summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Layer 1B expansion found a narrow set of US-listed direct or near-direct exposures. The highest-fit underfollowed candidate is HealthStream, which maps directly to healthcare workforce learning, credentialing, compliance, clinical development, and student-to-workforce infrastructure. Grand Canyon Education and Covista are direct healthcare-education asset/customer platforms investing in simulation, VR, licensure-linked degrees, and AI certificates. VirTra is a speculative micro-cap shadow candidate because it supplies immersive simulation and certified curriculum for regulated public-safety professions rather than healthcare education specifically. CAE was not included because recent search evidence indicates its healthcare segment became a former segment after the 2024 sale of the Healthcare business, weakening current direct node exposure. Public-market exposure clusters around two chokepoints: regulated exam/testing infrastructure and credential-rich workforce training platforms. The clearest anchor is Pearson VUE/Certiport as licensure and certification infrastructure. Grand Canyon Education and Stride/MedCerts show that healthcare and career education operators are explicitly buying simulation, VR, and AI-enhanced training capacity. Coursera is the smaller-cap discovery name: its AI/professional-certificate and verified-learning platform makes it the most underfollowed public exposure in this node.
